title: Vague prompt vs spec-quality prompt
goal: Implement the same date-range parser twice with the same agent: once from a one-line vague prompt, once from a prompt with context, constraints, examples and a done-when. Then compare the two diffs and run the hidden edge-case tests against both. Setup creates two copies, ex-1-2-vague (no SPEC.md) and ex-1-2-precise, each with a committed baseline.

starter_prompts.claude: Implement parseDateRange in @src/parseDateRange.ts exactly as described in @SPEC.md. First add tests in test/spec.test.ts for every input form and every error case in the spec, run them and watch them fail. Then implement. Do not edit test/basic.test.ts and add no dependencies. Done when `npm test` passes.
starter_prompts.codex: Implement parseDateRange in @src/parseDateRange.ts exactly as described in @SPEC.md. First add tests in test/spec.test.ts for every input form and every error case in the spec, run them and watch them fail. Then implement. Do not edit test/basic.test.ts and add no dependencies. Done when `npm test` passes.

solution_notes: The vague prompt has no way to learn about `this month`, the exact error messages or the `last 0 days` rule. Those requirements live only in SPEC.md, so a vague attempt cannot meet them however capable the agent is. The gap you measure is information, not intelligence.

The precise prompt supplies a done-when the agent can execute. It writes a test for every rule, sees them fail, then implements. Tests written from the spec catch the leap-year and month-boundary bugs before you do.

The reference solution does date arithmetic on UTC day numbers and round-trips each parsed date to reject impossible days such as 2026-02-30. `Date.UTC` silently rolls those over to March, which is the classic bug a vague implementation contains.

`today` is a parameter, so the function has no hidden dependency on the clock or time zone and the tests are deterministic. That constraint is one line in the prompt and prevents a whole class of flaky tests.
setup_cmd: if [ -e ~/fm-ex/ex-1-2-vague ] || [ -e ~/fm-ex/ex-1-2-precise ]; then echo "Already set up in ~/fm-ex. Run: cd ~/fm-ex/ex-1-2-vague (or ex-1-2-precise), or delete both folders to start over."; else mkdir -p ~/fm-ex && cp -R exercises/ex-1-2-vague-vs-precise/starter ~/fm-ex/ex-1-2-precise && cp -R exercises/ex-1-2-vague-vs-precise/starter ~/fm-ex/ex-1-2-vague && rm ~/fm-ex/ex-1-2-vague/SPEC.md && for d in ex-1-2-vague ex-1-2-precise; do (cd ~/fm-ex/$d && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.name=learner -c user.email=learner@example.com commit -qm start && npm install); done; fi
